Definition: from G138; properly, a choice, i.e. (specially) a party or (abstractly) disunion:--heresy (which is the Greek word itself), sect.
BiblicalUsage: In the New Testament, haíresis is the word for heresy (which is the Greek word itself), sect. In Acts 5:17, the text says "which is the sect of the Sadducees." In 1 Corinthians 11:19, the text says "that they which are approved may be made manifest among you."
TheologicalSignificance: My position is simple: haíresis tells me that false teaching sounds close to true, and that is what makes it dangerous. That shapes how I read the passages where it appears: not as filler, but as God's own wording for what He is doing.
